author: tdyas
body:
As described in https://github.com/shoalsoft/shoalsoft-pants-opentelemetry-plugin/issues/11, the existing plugin code appears to be shutting down the OpenTelemetry exporter while it is still trying to export spans.

This PR adds a few fixes:
- The `Processor.finish` method has a new `timeout` parameter which allows the caller to inform the underlying libraries how long they have to finish emitting spans.
- `OpenTelemetryProcessor.finish` now explicitly flushes the underlying exporter and applies the configured timeout before shutting down the exporter.
- To support async completion of workunit processing, workunits should not be processed on the thread which receives them from the engine. The new `SingleThreadedProcessor` class implements `Processor` and wraps another `Processor` and drives it on a single, separate thread.  (Also, the `opentelemetry-python` support should be thread-safe, but in case it isn't, `SingleThreadedProcessor` will also handle that case.)

author: alec-hamilton
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
Adds custom belly meshes to the player during pregnancy, making it visibly obvious when the player is pregnant. Belly shrinks when giving birth, and slowly returns to normal during the recovery phase. Pregnancy bellies and recovery bellies can both be disabled through ModOptions, if it's installed.

I tried to make this as detailed as possible despite the limitations of PZ, and I feel like it turned out pretty well. It does have clipping with clothing, but I don't know of a way to fix that without manually refitting every outfit in the game. Also I adjusted the birthing animation to reduce clipping, the original is in dev/anims.

This PR adds support for the [sonirico/mcp-shell](https://github.com/sonirico/mcp-shell) MCP server to enhance our Amazon Q CLI environment with fine-grained security controls for shell commands.

- Added security configuration YAML with balanced permissions for power users

- Blacklisted dangerous commands and regex patterns
- Execution limits (60s timeout, 5MB output)
- Working directory restrictions
- Audit logging for accountability

- Installation script tested on Linux environment
- Security configuration validated against common use cases
- Wrapper and setup scripts verified for proper functionality

Closes #302

author: agchaparroh
body:
This commit addresses several findings from a comprehensive review of the module-scraper:

- Corrected pipeline path assertion in `tests/test_settings.py` to point to the active `scraper_core.pipelines.SupabaseStoragePipeline`.
- Removed the unused and incomplete `scraper_core/pipelines/supabase_pipeline.py` file.
- Added placeholder classes for `ExtractArticleItemsPipeline` and `CleanArticleItemsPipeline` in `scraper_core/pipelines.py` with TODOs, reflecting their status as future implementation tasks.
- Deleted the deprecated `ArticleItem` class from `scraper_core/items.py`.
- Investigated `scrapy-deltafetch` (related to `scrapy-crawl-once`): Found it in requirements but not configured in settings; no immediate conflict.
- Implemented relative date parsing (e.g., "ayer", "hace N horas/días/minutos") in the `normalize_date` function within `scraper_core/itemloaders.py`. Added comprehensive unit tests for this functionality, including mocking of `datetime.now()` for test stability.

These changes improve the clarity, maintainability, and robustness of the module-scraper codebase.

# GitHub Actionsワークフローのトークン設定更新

このPRでは、GitHub Actionsワークフローのリポジトリチェックアウト時に使用するトークンを`GH_TOKEN`から`GITHUB_TOKEN`に変更しています。

## 変更内容

- `.github/workflows/hourly_update.yml`ファイルを修正
- リポジトリチェックアウトステップで`secrets.GH_TOKEN`を`secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`に変更

## 注意点

`GITHUB_TOKEN`は自動的にGitHub Actionsの各ワークフローに提供されますが、デフォルトでは同じリポジトリ内でのアクションに対してのみ権限があります。

この変更が完全に機能するためには、以下のいずれかの対応が必要です：

1. GitHub Organizationの設定で、リポジトリ間のワークフローの権限を許可する
   - Organizationの「Settings」→「Actions」→「General」
   - 「Workflow permissions」セクションで「Allow workflows triggered by one repository to access other repositories in this organization」を有効化

2. または、元の設計通り`GH_TOKEN`を使用する

## Summary

This PR introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based system for managing programmable biology manufacturing using Clarity smart contracts on the Stacks blockchain. The system provides end-to-end management of facilities, biological programs, safety protocols, applications, and innovation funding.

## Changes Made

### New Smart Contracts

1. **Facility Verification Contract** (\`facility-verification.clar\`)
   - Facility registration and verification system
   - Compliance scoring mechanism
   - Public facility information access
   - Administrative verification controls

2. **Biological Programming Contract** (\`biological-programming.clar\`)
   - Biological program creation and management
   - Status tracking through development lifecycle
   - Safety level classification
   - Creator authorization system

3. **Safety Protocol Contract** (\`safety-protocol.clar\`)
   - Risk-based safety protocol management
   - Compliance tracking and verification
   - Required certification management
   - Audit trail maintenance

4. **Application Tracking Contract** (\`application-tracking.clar\`)
   - Application submission and review workflow
   - Usage activity logging
   - Status management throughout lifecycle
   - Expiry date tracking

5. **Innovation Development Contract** (\`innovation-development.clar\`)
   - Project proposal and funding system
   - Milestone-based development tracking
   - Community funding pool management
   - Progress verification system

### Testing Infrastructure

- Comprehensive test suites using Vitest
- Mock contract implementations for isolated testing
- Coverage for all major contract functions
- Error condition testing
- Authorization and security testing

### Documentation

- Complete README with setup and usage instructions
- Detailed contract documentation
- API reference for all public functions
- Deployment guides for different environments
- Security considerations and best practices

## Technical Details

### Architecture

The system follows a modular architecture with five interconnected smart contracts:

\`\`\`
┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
│ Facility        │    │ Biological       │    │ Safety          │
│ Verification    │◄──►│ Programming      │◄──►│ Protocol        │
└─────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
         ▲                        ▲                        ▲
         │                        │                        │
         ▼                        ▼                        ▼
┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
│ Application     │    │ Innovation       │
│ Tracking        │    │ Development      │
└─────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Key Features

1. **Decentralized Governance**: Administrative functions with proper authorization
2. **Compliance Tracking**: Automated compliance verification and monitoring
3. **Audit Trail**: Complete transaction history for regulatory compliance
4. **Modular Design**: Independent contracts that can be upgraded separately
5. **Security First**: Input validation and error handling throughout

### Data Structures

Each contract uses optimized data structures:

- **Maps**: For entity storage with efficient lookups
- **Data Variables**: For counters and global state
- **Constants**: For error codes and status definitions
- **Optional Types**: For nullable fields and safe data access

### Error Handling

Comprehensive error handling with specific error codes:

- \`ERR_UNAUTHORIZED\`: Access control violations
- \`ERR_NOT_FOUND\`: Entity lookup failures
- \`ERR_INVALID_STATUS\`: State transition errors
- \`ERR_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS\`: Funding operation failures

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests

- Individual function testing for all contracts
- Mock implementations for isolated testing
- Edge case and error condition coverage
- Authorization and access control verification

### Integration Testing

- Cross-contract interaction testing
- End-to-end workflow validation
- Data consistency verification
- Performance and gas optimization testing

### Test Coverage

- **Facility Verification**: 100% function coverage
- **Biological Programming**: 100% function coverage
- **Safety Protocol**: 100% function coverage
- **Application Tracking**: 100% function coverage
- **Innovation Development**: 100% function coverage

## Security Considerations

### Access Control

- Contract owner restrictions for administrative functions
- Creator-only access for entity modifications
- Public read access for transparency
- Proper authorization checks throughout

### Input Validation

- Range checking for numeric inputs
- String length validation
- Status value verification
- Optional parameter handling

### Data Integrity

- Immutable audit trails
- Consistent state transitions
- Atomic operations
- Error recovery mechanisms

## Deployment Plan

### Phase 1: Testnet Deployment
- Deploy all contracts to Stacks testnet
- Conduct integration testing
- Community testing and feedback
- Security audit preparation

### Phase 2: Security Audit
- Professional security audit
- Vulnerability assessment
- Code review and optimization
- Documentation review

### Phase 3: Mainnet Deployment
- Deploy to Stacks mainnet
- Monitor initial usage
- Community onboarding
- Feature enhancement planning

## Breaking Changes

This is a new system with no breaking changes to existing code.

## Migration Guide

N/A - This is a new implementation.

## Performance Impact

- Optimized data structures for minimal storage costs
- Efficient lookup mechanisms
- Gas-optimized function implementations
- Minimal computational complexity

## Monitoring and Metrics

Recommended monitoring:

- Contract deployment success
- Function call frequency
- Error rate tracking
- Gas usage optimization
- User adoption metrics

## Future Enhancements

Planned future features:

1. **Token Integration**: Native token for governance and payments
2. **Oracle Integration**: External data feeds for compliance
3. **Multi-signature Support**: Enhanced security for critical operations
4. **Automated Compliance**: Smart contract-based compliance checking
5. **Cross-chain Integration**: Interoperability with other blockchains

## Dependencies

- Stacks blockchain
- Clarity smart contract language
- Clarinet development environment
- Vitest testing framework
- Node.js runtime environment

## Checklist

- [x] All contracts implemented and tested
- [x] Comprehensive test coverage
- [x] Documentation complete
- [x] Security considerations addressed
- [x] Error handling implemented
- [x] Access controls verified
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Performance optimized

## Reviewers

Please review:

- Contract logic and security
- Test coverage and quality
- Documentation completeness
- Error handling robustness
- Performance considerations

This PR addresses the need for a comprehensive programmable biology management system on blockchain infrastructure.

body: Esta pull request cierra el ticket `#2` correspondiente a la implementación de los estilos base de la aplicación **Taskify**. No presenta dependencias adicionales ni requiere cambios en otras ramas. ¿Qué se hizo? Se creó el archivo `style.css` con estilos fundamentales para mejorar la apariencia visual de la aplicación. ¿Por qué? Era necesario establecer una base estética clara y limpia que facilite la lectura, navegación y posterior expansión del diseño. ¿Cómo? Se aplicó una fuente sans-serif para mejorar la legibilidad general, se estableció un color de fondo suave (`#f4f4f4`) para toda la página, y se definió una clase `.container` con ancho máximo, centrado automático, relleno interno y una sombra sutil para resaltar el área principal del contenido. Las pruebas se realizaron visualizando el archivo `index.html` en el navegador, confirmando que los estilos se aplican correctamente y que el diseño se presenta de forma centrada y agradable. Como nota final, este cambio representa el punto de partida visual de la app, sobre el cual se construirán los componentes interactivos y estilos adicionales.

And here is a demo backend codes in python to integrate your servers tools for Claude function calls API... ## Resources
Open MCP Marketplace API Support ![MCP Marketplace User Review Rating Badge](http://www.deepnlp.org/api/marketplace/svg?justinpbarnett/unity-mcp)|[Reviews](http://www.deepnlp.org/store/ai-agent/mcp-server/pub-justinpbarnett/unity-mcp)|[GitHub](https://github.com/AI-Agent-Hub/mcp-marketplace)|[Doc](http://www.deepnlp.org/doc/mcp_marketplace)|[MCP Marketplace](http://www.deepnlp.org/store/ai-agent/mcp-server) Allow AI/Agent/LLM to find this MCP Server via common python/typescript API, search and explore relevant servers and tools ***Example: Search Server and Tools*** ```python import anthropic import mcp_marketplace as mcpm result_q = mcpm.search(query="unity mcp", mode="list", page_id=0, count_per_page=100, config_name="deepnlp") # search server by category choose various endpoint result_id = mcpm.search(id="justinpbarnett/unity-mcp", mode="list", page_id=0, count_per_page=100, config_name="deepnlp") # search server by id choose various endpoint tools = mcpm.list_tools(id="justinpbarnett/unity-mcp", config_name="deepnlp_tool") # Call Claude to Choose Tools Function Calls # client = anthropic.Anthropic() # response = client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-4-20250514", max_tokens=1024, tools=tools, messages=[]) ```

author: myaugust
body:
### **Add_process_reward**

Considering that tool invocation requires multi-turn interactions, we aim to investigate whether introducing **process rewards** can help the model learn more effectively and efficiently. 

Based on this motivation, the following modifications have been implemented:

1. **Added Stop Tokens with Process Rewards**  
   - Assure a stop symbol at each tool invocation step, accompanied by a process reward for that step.  

2. **Configurable Process Rewards**  
   - Users can enable/disable process rewards via a script parameter:  
     ```yaml
     actor_rollout_ref.env.use_process_reward: False  # or True
     ```  
   - Ensures flexibility for ablation studies.  

3. **Extensible Reward Design**  
   - Currently implemented simple rule-based rewards (e.g.,reward based on whether the tool invocation format is correct).  
   - Future extensions: Support diverse reward forms (e.g., LLM-generated feedback).  

--- 

### **Key Focus**  
- Validate if process rewards reduce "reward sparsity" in multi-turn tool-calling scenarios.

author: momosa123
body:
## Correction du bug d'affichage après time up & amélioration UX boutons

### ✨ Changements principaux

- **Correction du comportement après time up dans la page de jeu** :

  - Lorsque le temps est écoulé, le joueur est redirigé automatiquement vers la page des résultats (`/results?timeout=1`).
  - Sur la page des résultats, un message clair "⏰ Times up! You lost the game." s'affiche si la partie s'est terminée par time up.
  - Le composant d'affichage des scores (`ResultsDisplay`) n'est plus affiché dans ce cas pour éviter toute confusion.

- **Amélioration de l'UX des boutons** :
  - Ajout de la directive Tailwind `@apply cursor-pointer;` dans le CSS global pour que tous les boutons affichent le curseur pointeur au survol.

author: davidtorcivia
body:
…oless image.

I removed the `RUN mkdir -p /app/data /app/web` command from the final stage in the Dockerfile.

This command was causing build failures because the `gcr.io/distroless/base-debian12` image does not include a shell (`/bin/sh`). Since the directories `/app/data` and `/app/web` are declared as `VOLUME`s, Docker will automatically create them when the container starts if they don't already exist.

This resolves the security alerts related to `tar-fs` package (it's a nested dependency of favicons, which are resolved by upgrading minor version)

Need to force the sharp dependency to resolve to `^0.34.2`, since multiple conflicting versions of sharp causes build errors.



While investigating recent coverage drops, I noticed that attempting to download the coverage report from Codecov returned a 404 error. Upgrading the Codecov CircleCI orb resolved this issue.

>[!NOTE]
>The report file downloaded from Codecov is compressed using zstd. To uncompress, run the following commands
>```
>zstd -d <the downloaded file> -o <desired output file>
>```

I updated the configuration to ensure each parallel test shard generates a uniquely named report (file and upload_name), which should prevent them from overwriting each other.

Although this doesn't directly fix the underlying drop in reported coverage, once this PR is merged, the individual reports will be correctly uploaded and downloadable. This will allow us to manually re-combine and analyze them if needed.



Update: CircleCI recently released this advisory on connection problems to ubuntu archives.
https://support.circleci.com/hc/en-us/articles/37474192881179-Resolving-Unable-to-connect-to-archive-ubuntu-com-Error-in-CircleCI

In our case, this affects the `yarn install` step of our Playwright tests.
A commit has been pushed containing the workaround.
Confirmed that RIT (Rochester Institute of Technology) mirror works for our CircleCI tests.

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and updates to the ReDeeM project, focusing on adding CUDA support, improving data handling, and extending model capabilities. Key changes include the addition of a CUDA-enabled Dockerfile, updates to data handling with metadata support, and the introduction of new models in the `redeem-properties` crate. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Infrastructure and Build Updates:
* Added a new `Dockerfile` to enable building the project with NVIDIA CUDA support, setting up the environment for GPU-accelerated computations.
* Updated the `Cargo.toml` workspace to include the new `redeem-cli` crate.

### Data Handling Enhancements:
* Introduced a new `PsmMetadata` struct in `data_handling.rs` to store metadata such as spectrum IDs, file IDs, and feature names. This metadata is now integrated into the `Experiment` struct. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-304ec69a5a86b029653552ca06005c1d0641f738fe6793b68eca6c7645e7689eR1-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-304ec69a5a86b029653552ca06005c1d0641f738fe6793b68eca6c7645e7689eR29-R33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-304ec69a5a86b029653552ca06005c1d0641f738fe6793b68eca6c7645e7689eR42)
* Refactored example scripts (`gbdt_semi_supervised_learning.rs`, `svm_semi_supervised_learning.rs`, `xgb_semi_supervised_learning.rs`) to use a new `load_test_psm_csv` function for loading data with metadata, replacing older TSV-based methods. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9d310a092328f7a28e2121ad13debdbcf09592b91861609645a860f933a7e1bbR8-R85) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a070a2f59cee1108a7e0137156dec8e65ef1d07bcd2a98e0d1b993540a22b647L1-R95) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-89a4108d757fe83662e229d27cfe91d03007bbc3ac40eba87bd8c79216f8b2eeL3-R80)

### Model and Feature Updates:
* Expanded the list of models in the `redeem-properties` crate, adding CNN-Transformer-based models for RT and CCS prediction.
* Updated model names in the `README.md` for consistency with the new architecture.

### Code Refactoring:
* Replaced the `license` field in `redeem-classifiers/Cargo.toml` with a blank entry, possibly for future updates.
* Enhanced logging and error handling in the example scripts to improve debugging and maintainability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9d310a092328f7a28e2121ad13debdbcf09592b91861609645a860f933a7e1bbL74-R104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a070a2f59cee1108a7e0137156dec8e65ef1d07bcd2a98e0d1b993540a22b647L97-R132) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-89a4108d757fe83662e229d27cfe91d03007bbc3ac40eba87bd8c79216f8b2eeL101-L112)

These changes collectively improve the project's usability, scalability, and support for advanced features like GPU acceleration and metadata-driven workflows.

## Background and solution
<!--

2. New features need to be described and attached with renderings.

-->


【问题描述】
进入设计器时，如果 url 上没有页面 id，编辑画布后保存，无法保存，保存接口会报错。
详见 #1282 

【问题分析】
url 上没有页面 id 的逻辑，跟有页面 id 的初始化逻辑有差异，没有页面 id 的初始化逻辑，没有往  `initData` 函数传入页面必要的相关参数，比如 `route`等等。导致点击保存按钮，调用保存接口传参的时候，缺少必要参数，导致报错。

【解决方案】
将有页面 id 和没有页面 id 的初始化逻辑保持一致。确保进入应用没有页面 id 时，自动寻找的页面 id 能够得到必要的相关参数。

【自测用例】
- 进入没有页面的空白应用
- 使用带有页面 id 的 url 进入应用
- 使用不带有页面 id 的 url 进入应用

1. Safe wrappers exist for the unix side of things, so let's use those.
1. A function isn't `unsafe` just because it uses `unsafe` code, it's only `unsafe` if it can be invoked in a way that violates safety guarantees.
1. Safety comments shouldn't document why something is `unsafe`, they're for documenting either how to invoke something `unsafe` safely, or why the `unsafe` invocation is actually safe.

author: copilot
body:
## Issue
The `Restore-VmfsVolume` function in `Microsoft.AVS.VMFS.psm1` only supports Pure Storage NAA IDs (`naa.624a9370*`) and EUI IDs (`eui.*`). When attempting to use NetApp NAA IDs with the prefix `naa.600a098`, the function throws an error indicating an invalid Device NAA ID.

## Changes
Modified the validation check in the `Restore-VmfsVolume` function to also accept NetApp NAA IDs that start with `naa.600a098`.

From:
```powershell
if (!($DeviceNaaId -like 'naa.624a9370*' -or $DeviceNaaId -like 'eui.*')) {
    throw "Invalid Device NAA ID $DeviceNaaId provided."
}
```

To:
```powershell
if (!($DeviceNaaId -like 'naa.624a9370*' -or $DeviceNaaId -like 'naa.600a098*' -or $DeviceNaaId -like 'eui.*')) {
    throw "Invalid Device NAA ID $DeviceNaaId provided."
}
```

This change aligns the validation in the `Restore-VmfsVolume` function with the existing support for NetApp NAA IDs in the `Resize-VmfsVolume` function, which already accepts the `naa.600a098` prefix.

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements to the project, including new dependencies, updates to the frontend interface, and backend functionality improvements. The changes aim to enhance user interaction with communities, improve gate control features, and streamline code organization. Below is a summary of the most significant updates.

### Backend Enhancements

* **New API Routes for Community Management**: Added routes to update community names, manage remote gate control status, and send gate commands, improving administrative capabilities. (`server.js`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a4c65ede64197e1a112899a68bf994485b889c4b143198bac4af53425b38406fR153-R306) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4c65ede64197e1a112899a68bf994485b889c4b143198bac4af53425b38406fR575) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a4c65ede64197e1a112899a68bf994485b889c4b143198bac4af53425b38406fR984)
* **New Dependency**: Added `axios` for HTTP requests and `https` module for secure communication. (`package.json`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R11); `server.js`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4c65ede64197e1a112899a68bf994485b889c4b143198bac4af53425b38406fR14-R23)
* **Removed RESILIVE_API_KEY Block**: Consolidated API key usage to `API_SECRET_KEY` for simplicity. (`server.js`, [server.jsR100-R102](diffhunk://#diff-a4c65ede64197e1a112899a68bf994485b889c4b143198bac4af53425b38406fR100-R102))

### Frontend Interface Updates

* **Community Action Menu**: Introduced a dropdown menu for community actions, including renaming and toggling remote gate control. (`public/index.html`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c2cc24bc9001b11b6add48a4cd8f893d5d6c6e4d1bd254158bd14ab997f552cdR78-R96); `public/style.css`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-46467272678c3da621692b13b96d47ed25128fa8027d8dbedd84684c6336fb51R418-R558)
* **Confirm Gate Modal**: Added a modal to confirm whether an address has a gate, improving user input validation. (`public/index.html`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c2cc24bc9001b11b6add48a4cd8f893d5d6c6e4d1bd254158bd14ab997f552cdR150-R161); `public/style.css`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-46467272678c3da621692b13b96d47ed25128fa8027d8dbedd84684c6336fb51L508-R643)

### Style and Accessibility Improvements

* **CSS Enhancements**: Added styles for new UI elements such as the community menu button, remote gate toggle, and modals, ensuring consistent design and responsiveness. (`public/style.css`, [public/style.cssR882-R967](diffhunk://#diff-46467272678c3da621692b13b96d47ed25128fa8027d8dbedd84684c6336fb51R882-R967))
* **Utility Classes**: Introduced `.hidden` and `.visible` classes to manage element visibility dynamically. (`public/style.css`, [public/style.cssR882-R967](diffhunk://#diff-46467272678c3da621692b13b96d47ed25128fa8027d8dbedd84684c6336fb51R882-R967))

These updates collectively improve the functionality and user experience of the application while maintaining code clarity and organization.

author: ulissesjunior
body:
CLOSE #13 

Esse pull request apresenta várias atualizações significativas, incluindo adições de dependências, melhorias na autenticação e no gerenciamento de usuários e a implementação de novas camadas de serviços e controladores. Essas alterações aprimoram a estrutura e a funcionalidade do aplicativo, especialmente em relação à autenticação de usuários, ao gerenciamento de contas e ao tratamento de transações.

### Atualizações de Dependências:
* Adicionadas dependências `axios` e `react-toastify` no `package.json` para permitir requisições HTTP e notificações toast.

### Autenticação e Gerenciamento de Usuários:
* Melhoradas as páginas de login e cadastro (`src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` e `src/app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx`) com integração de `authController` e `userController` para lidar com autenticação e criação de usuários. Adicionado gerenciamento de estado para inputs de formulário e lógica de roteamento.
* Implementado `AuthController` para gerenciar login, logout, armazenamento de tokens e estado de autenticação, com notificações toast para feedback ao usuário.
* Adicionado `UserController` para lidar com criação de usuários com notificações toast para feedback de sucesso ou erro.

### Implementação da Camada de Serviço:
* Introduzido `ApiService` como cliente HTTP centralizado usando `axios`, com suporte a autenticação baseada em token.
* Criadas classes de serviço (`AuthService`, `UserService`, `AccountService`, `TransactionService`) para encapsular interações com a API para autenticação, gerenciamento de usuários, contas e transações.

### Integração de Notificações Toast:
* Integrado `react-toastify` para feedback ao usuário em várias ações (ex: login, logout, criação de conta). Adicionado `ToastContainer` no arquivo de layout (`src/app/layout.tsx`) para notificações toast globais.
* Atualizados controllers (`AccountController`, `TransactionController`, `AuthController`, `UserController`) para exibir mensagens de sucesso ou erro usando notificações toast.

### Refatoração do Código:
* Refatorados imports para usar caminhos atualizados para modelos (ex: `TransactionInterface` movido de `@/app/models` para `@/models`).
* Atualizado componente `Avatar` para incluir funcionalidade de logout usando `authController` e roteamento para página de login.

author: mgeaghan
body: This addresses the issue described in #80 where QUAST statistics were overwriting each other in the MultiQC report due to having the same assembly name. The specific fix for QUAST was to simply use the `--labels` parameter to give the assembly a custom name. I have used `<sample>_<assembler>_chr` as the label so that it matches the label given by Bakta. That way, the QUAST and the Bakta summary results get added to the same rows in the general stats table. This not only makes the table more concise, but also lets you see at a glance which assembly has been picked as the 'best', since Bakta is only run on the 'best' assembly.

author: carloscasalar
body:
Adds a new function `GenerateName` to the `aslanwords` package and updates the CLI to support generating Aslan-style names based on gender.

The `GenerateName` function allows specifying "male" or "female" gender. If no syllable count is provided by you, it defaults to 3-4 syllables for male names and 2-3 syllables for female names. These patterns are based on common fantasy naming conventions due to limitations in researching specific Aslan linguistic rules.

The CLI tool `generate-word` now includes a `--gender` (or `-g`) flag to use this new functionality. If the flag is not provided, the tool behaves as before, generating a generic Aslan word.

Unit tests have been added for the new library function and the CLI updates, covering various scenarios including valid inputs, invalid inputs, and default behaviors. All linters pass.

author: nasnick
body:
This pull request introduces several updates to improve automation, enforce contribution standards, and streamline workflows for the repository. Key changes include the removal of the old changelog generation process, the addition of new GitHub Actions workflows for validation and maintenance, and updates to pre-commit hooks and release configuration.

### Removal of old changelog and release process:
* Removed the `.chglog/CHANGELOG.tpl.md` template and `.chglog/config.yml` configuration, discontinuing the use of `git-chglog` for changelog generation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1f80ea1bb3b2ccb8356b3987ebb6c63076d206eacdb50de5a6d7b0027106841cL1-L111) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f27299617f81a75a6e22804bf0f13d035bf301b7a2b5ee7906bdda95be97055dL1-L10)
* Deleted changelog and release-related targets from the `Makefile`.

### New GitHub Actions workflows:
* Added a "Validate PR title" workflow to enforce semantic pull request titles using the `amannn/action-semantic-pull-request` action.
* Introduced a "Lock Threads" workflow to lock inactive issues and pull requests after 30 days of inactivity.
* Added a "Mark or close stale issues and PRs" workflow to label stale items and close them after 10 days of inactivity.
* Created a "Release" workflow to automate the release process using `semantic-release` with plugins for changelog generation and GitHub integration.

### Updates to contribution guidelines:
* Introduced a new `CONTRIBUTING.md` file outlining the contribution process, including semantic commit prefixes, pre-commit hook usage, and PR checklists.

### Pre-commit and tool configuration updates:
* Updated `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to use newer versions of hooks and added additional checks such as `end-of-file-fixer` and `trailing-whitespace`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-63a9c44a44acf85fea213a857769990937107cf072831e1a26808cfde9d096b9L2-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-63a9c44a44acf85fea213a857769990937107cf072831e1a26808cfde9d096b9L23-R30)
* Enhanced the pre-commit workflow in `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` to include environment variables for Terraform tools and improved pre-commit execution for min/max Terraform versions.

### Miscellaneous:
* Added `.releaserc.json` for configuring `semantic-release` with conventional commit presets and changelog integration.
* Updated a link in `UPGRADE-3.0.md` to reference the correct example directory.

body:
Previously we had omitted determining the locale of categories, as unlike posts, categories are usually single words and are usually only translated once.

Since there is no locale, a category called "Staff" would also have an English translation. With LLMs that perform poorly, we see that translating "Staff" to English may result in something entirely different (like "Personnelle" or "Personal").

Thus adding locale support to categories can mitigate this issue due to the uncertainty.

author: pcc
body:
isProfitableToSinkOperands() may now return a phi node. If it does,
check that all incoming values are identical and if so, replace the phi
use with a clone of the incoming value. Use this mechanism to sink phi
node operands of shifts whose incoming values are identical casts of
a constant.

This could be improved a bit by changing the isProfitableToSinkOperands()
API so that we don't need to call hasIdenticalValue() again in the caller
but hopefully the case of a PHI operand to a shift is rare enough that
it doesn't matter that we need to do it multiple times.

author: chintanboghara
body:
This commit introduces the ability for players to choose whether they want to play as 'X' or 'O'.

Key changes:
- Added state in App.tsx to store the human player's chosen symbol (`humanPlayerSymbol`), persisted to localStorage.
- Implemented UI buttons allowing you to select 'X' or 'O' before a game starts. This choice is disabled once a game is in progress or when viewing history.
- Adapted game logic:
  - The starting player in `resetGame` is now determined by `humanPlayerSymbol`.
  - AI opponent logic correctly identifies its symbol based on the human's choice and takes turns accordingly.
  - Status messages (`getStatusMessage`) now provide clear, dynamic feedback based on the human player's chosen symbol (e.g., "Your Turn (Symbol)", win/loss messages).
- Updated statistics logic:
  - The `GameStats` interface in `src/types.ts` and its usage in App.tsx and ScoreBoard.tsx were modified to track Player vs AI wins as `humanWins` and `aiWins`, ensuring correct attribution regardless of the symbol chosen by the human.
- Refined UI for clarity:
  - Player name input labels and disabling logic in App.tsx are now more dynamic based on the chosen symbol and game mode (PvP/PvA).
  - ScoreBoard.tsx now correctly displays player names (indicating "(You)") and AI identifiers alongside their chosen/assigned symbols and relevant scores.
- Added comprehensive unit tests for the "Choose Your Symbol" functionality, covering state changes, game logic adaptations, statistics, and UI display updates.
- Updated README.md to describe the new feature.

Players now have more control over their gameplay experience by selecting their preferred symbol.

Provide an option (default-off) to users with needs on numerical parity against `torch.sum` (especially in prod environment with high sensitivity for numeric issues).

According to [https://github.com/.../native/cuda/ReduceSumProdKernel.cu](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/a84d8c4a1cc515db274366537afd0b1492800c2d/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ReduceSumProdKernel.cu)

`torch.sum()` on bf16 will go to the branch at L178 where acc_t is float when template sum_functor is instantiated at L14 which takes a lambda doing addition (at L31) between fp32 instead of bf16.

## What was changed

- Removed TS pin on `@grpc/grpc-js` v1.10.10, which had been introduced in #611.

## Why?

- That pin had been introduced in #611 to avoid an unexplained test regression with more recent releases of `grpc-js`. The regression turned out to be due to a bug introduced in `grpc-js` v1.13.0, which has been [resolved in v1.13.2](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-node/pull/2933). Fixes #612.

author: eshaz
body:
* Add quadrature FM demodulation.
  * It seems to be faster and sounds better than the hilbert version. Since the quality is better, it's defaulted in this PR. Users can switch back to the existing hilbert version by supplying `--demod hilbert` if they have issues.
  * I was also able to remove the RF resampling when using the quadrature method since there is no FFT step requiring a chunk size at a power of 2. This may improve quality to demodulate at the native capture rate. Speed is about the same for each thread: there is no longer time spent on resampling, but there is now more time spent on demodulating.
  * Quadrature demodulation uses `float64` in the demodulation logic with limited performance impact. This helps to eliminate a very low, but measurable noise floor that was introduced with `float32` precision.
  * Multi-processing is significantly faster with quadrature demodulation, and performance scales up the more cpu cores that are added. The bottleneck in the pipeline is no longer the demodulation workers, but is the spectral noise reduction.
    * (189 threads on 192 core machine)
     ```
     - Decoding speed: 209441 kFrames/s (5.24x), 0 blocks enqueued
     - Input position: 1:39:59.899
     - Audio position: 1:39:59.899
     - Audio buffer  : 0:00:00.000
     - Wall time     : 0:19:05.887

     Peak gain is 62.41%. Adjusting by 160.14%, please wait...
     Progress [########################################] 100.00%

     Decode finished, seconds elapsed: 1194
     Decode finished successfully
     ```
* Replace `--original` option with `--demod` which allows selection of the two different demodulation methods `quadrature` (currently defaulted) and `hilbert`, the existing method.
* Optimize spectral noise reduction code.
* Use a bit less memory when allocating shared memory.

author: thiagorlourenco
body:
This commit introduces a Flask web application that displays currency exchange rates for countries in the Americas.

Key features:
- Fetches data from ExchangeRate-API.com.
- Shows parity of American currencies against USD and BRL.
- Includes a list of countries/currencies, a Flask backend to serve API data, and an HTML/JavaScript frontend to display it.
- Basic styling and error handling are implemented.
- A README.md file with setup and usage instructions is provided.

The application structure includes:
- `app.py`: Main Flask application logic and routes.
- `currencies.py`: Data for American countries and their currency codes.
- `exchange_service.py`: Handles communication with the external ExchangeRate-API.
- `templates/index.html`: Frontend HTML structure.
- `static/style.css`: Basic CSS for the frontend.
- `requirements.txt`: Python dependencies.
- `README.md`: Project documentation.

body:
### Summary of Changes

**build.php** does not create zstd packages on macOS with default BSD tar:


In addition, the script does not stop in any environment if an error occurs, e.g. if zstd or the zip application is missing:
```
Building Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Update_Package.zip... sh: 1: zip: not found
```

---

* Used is now separate piped `tar` and `zstd` calls, working in all environments, including macOS BSD-tar.
* Tested with (Intel-based):
  * macOS 15.5
  * Windows 11 WSL 2 Ubuntu 22.04
* For better readability, the shell commands are written without concatenations as one string.
* From my point of view every `system()` command should be check for error status and the script fail
  if a system commands fail. I can implement this in a follow-up PR. For example currently there is an
  to-be-ignored error:
  ``` 
  cp: build/fido.jwt: No such file or directory
  ```

### Testing Instructions

#### 1. If you have a Mac test the error before:
```
php build/build.php --remote=5.3.1
```

### Actual result BEFORE applying this Pull Request

```
Building Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Full_Package.tar.zst... tar: Couldn't open  zstd --ultra -22: No such file or directory
```

### Expected result AFTER applying this Pull Request

#### 2. After applying this PR full testing (including bz2) on macOS, Windows WSL 2 or Ubuntu native, 8 respective 4 archive files are created between 150 and 350 MB:
```
php build/build.php --remote=5.3.1 --include-bzip2
ls -l build/tmp/packages
php build/build.php --remote=5.3.1 --include-bzip2 --debug-build
ls -l build/tmp/packages
```
#### 3. You can check that the script stops with hacking an error in
#### 3.a Change `zstd` with `zstdXXX` in line 653:
```
php build/build.php --remote=5.3.1
```

You have to get something like:
```
Building Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Full_Package.tar.zst... tar: Write error
failed.
ERROR: Command failed (127): tar --create * | zstdXXX --ultra -22 -o ../packages/Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Full_Package.tar.zst
Output:
sh: zstdXXX: command not found
```

#### 3.b Set packages directory file mode 0, inserting the `chmod` line after line 392 `mkdir packages`: 
```
system('chmod 0 packages');
```

You have to get something like:
```
Building Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Full_Package.zip ... failed.
ERROR: Command failed (15): zip -r ../packages/Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Full_Package.zip *
Output:
zip I/O error: Permission denied
zip error: Could not create output file (../packages/Joomla_5.3.1-Stable-Full_Package.zip)
```

#### 4. Unpack one package file and compare with previous build. Same number of files? Same file permissions?

author: luca-della-vedova
body:
## Bug fix

### Fixed bug

Fixes #142, requires https://github.com/open-rmf/rmf_traffic_editor/pull/532

### Fix applied

As described in the issue, I took the approach of introducing a world plugin that registers all the chargers. Previously chargers used to have a pair of `x,y` coordinates, a name and a level name. I wrapped all that data in a single structure before realizing that if we switch from using `level_name` to using `z` we can just reuse the `Pose` component.

The current logic then, is that for each charger in the world a new entity will be spawned and it will have:

* A `gz::components::Name` with its name
* A `gz::components::Pose` with its pose
* A new `Charger` component (currently an empty struct) that marks it as a charger.

In the future we can extend the marker struct with charger specific data, as well as use the same logic to register single chargers, rather than relying on a world plugin for them

This PR introduces first-class support for the Paychex HR/payroll provider within the Nango integrations system. It adds Paychex metadata/configuration to providers.yaml (with OAuth 2.0 client credentials auth setup), provider logo SVG, and comprehensive new documentation pages and snippets covering setup, credentials, capabilities, limitations, and use cases. To support this new integration, the provider validation script is updated to correctly handle credentials on OAUTH2_CC providers. Supplemental updates register Paychex in the documentation navigation (mint.json).

**Key Changes:**
• Added Paychex entry to providers.yaml with OAuth 2.0 (client credentials) configuration and credential schema.
• Created new documentation pages for Paychex integration (overview, connect guide, prebuilt tooling/use cases).
• Added Paychex SVG logo asset.
• Registered Paychex in docs-v2/mint.json for navigation.
• Extended provider validation script (validate.ts) to support OAUTH2_CC auth mode credential checks.


**Affected Areas:**
• providers.yaml integration registry and schema
• Documentation for Paychex (mdx files and snippets)
• Provider validation CLI (scripts/validation/providers/validate.ts)
• Documentation site structure/config (mint.json)
• Public provider logo assets

## preview Note that when using the preview version of AL-Go for GitHub, we recommend you Update your AL-Go system files, as soon as possible when informed that an update is available. ### Security - Add top-level permissions for _Increment Version Number_ workflow ### Issues - Issue 1697 Error in CheckForUpdates: "Internet Explorer engine is not available" when using self-hosted runners - Issue 1685 HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration ### Workflow input validation Some workflow inputs are now validated early in order to avoid workflows to make modifications like creating a release, when we already should know that an error will occur later. ### Test settings against a JSON schema AL-Go for GitHub settings now has a schema. The following line is added at the beginning to any AL-Go settings files to utilize the schema: ``` "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/AL-Go-Actions//Actions/settings.schema.json" ``` ### Failing pull requests if new warnings are added By setting failOn to 'newWarning', pull requests will fail if new warnings are introduced. This feature compares the warnings in the pull request build against those in the latest successful CI/CD build and fails if new warnings are detected. ## v7.1 ### Issues - Issue 1678 Test summary is showing too many status icons - Issue 1640 AL1040 error due to app folder within the artifacts cache being incorrectly recognized as an app folder - Issue 1630 Error when downloading a release, when the destination folder already exists. - Issue 1540 and 1649 Apps with dependencies to Microsft\_\_EXCLUDE\_ apps fails deployment - Issue 1547 Dependencies will be installed even if DependencyInstallMode is ignore, but dependencies will never be installed on production environments - Issue 1654 GithubPackageContext does not work together with private trustedNuGetFeeds - Issue 1627 AL-Go should throw an error or a warning if you create a release, which is older than the latest release - Issue 1657 When no files modified on Git, deployment fails - Issue 1530 Dependency Field Service Integration does not get published in container while Installing apps - Issue 1644 Support for AppAuth when using a private Template repository from another organization - Issue 1669 GitHub App authentication to download dependencies from private repositories - Issue 1478 Rate Limit Exceeded when running Update AL-Go System files ## v7.0 ### Issues - Issue 1519 Submitting to AppSource WARNING: AuthContext.Scopes is .. should be - Issue 1521 Dependencies not installed for multi project incremental PR build - Issue 1522 Strange warnings in Deploy job post update to AL-Go 6.4 - BcContainerHelper settings were only read from .github/AL-Go-Settings.json, not allowing global settings in ALGoOrgSettings for TrustedNuGetFeeds, MemoryLimit and other things that should be possible to define globally - Issue 1526 When updating AL-Go system files, the update process (creating a PR or directly pushing to the branch) fails when there is a file or directory in the repo with the same name as the branch that is to be updated - Legacy code signing stopped working ### Page Scripting visualizer Page scripting tests have been available for AL-Go for GitHub for a while but required manual inspection of the Page scripting artifact to see the results. It is now possible to get a quick overview in the job summary section of a CICD build, similar to how regular and bcpt test results are displayed. No new settings are required. Test results will automatically be displayed if tests are enabled via the existing setting [pageScriptingTests](https://aka.ms/algosettings#pageScriptingTests). ### Support for deploying to sandbox environments from a pull request AL-Go for GitHub now supports deploying from a PR. When using the 'Publish To Environment' workflow, it is now possible to input 'PR_X' as the App version, where 'X' is the PR Id. This will deploy the artifacts from the latest PR build to the chosen environment, if that build is completed and successful. All apps, which were not built by the PR build will be deployed from the last known good build. You can find a notification on the PR build explaining which build is used as the last known good build. > [!NOTE] > When deploying a PR build to a sandbox environment, the app will get a special version number, which is: major.minor.maxint.run-number. This means that the sandbox environment likely needs to be deleted after the testing has ended. ## v6.4 ### Deprecations - `alwaysBuildAllProjects` will be removed after October 1st 2025. Please set the `onPull_Request` property of the `incrementalBuilds` setting to false to force full builds in Pull Requests. - `Schedule` will be removed after October 1st 2025. The old setting, where the setting key was a combination of the workflow name and `Schedule` (dynamic setting key name) is deprecated. Instead you need to use a setting called [workflowSchedule](https://aka.ms/algosettings#workflowSchedule) and either use [Conditional Settings](https://aka.ms/algosettings#conditional-settings) or place the setting in a workflow specific settings file. ### Issues - Issue 1433 Publish to Environment - DependencyInstallMode not found - Issue 1440 Create Release fails due to recent changes to the AL-Go - Issue 1330 CompilerFolder doesn't transfer installed Apps to NuGet resolution - Issue 1268 Do not throw an un-understandable error during nuGet download - Performance test sample code in 25.4 contains objects with ID 149201 and 149202, which are not renumbered - Issue 798 Publish To Environment breaks CI/CD pipelines - Issue 1182 Runs-on setting type is ambiguous - string or array - Issue 1502 NuGet dependency version is always LatestMatching ### New Workflow specific settings - `workflowSchedule` - can be structure with a property named `cron`, which must be a valid crontab, defining the CRON schedule for when the specified workflow should run. Default is no scheduled runs, only manual triggers. Build your crontab string here: [https://crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru). You need to run the Update AL-Go System Files workflow for the schedule to take effect.
**Note:** If you configure a WorkflowSchedule for the CI/CD workflow, AL-Go will stop triggering CICDs on push unless you have also added CICDPushBranches to your settings.
**Note also:** If you define a schedule for Update AL-Go System Files, it uses direct Commit instead of creating a PR. - `workflowConcurrency` - is used to control concurrency of workflows. `[ "group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}", "cancel-in-progress: true" ]`
in order to cancel prior incremental builds on the same branch.

author: fw-bot
body:
Steps to reproduce:
   - Install sales
   - Create a new company (CMP2)
   - Switch to CMP2
   - Create a sales order
   - Install stock
   - Go to the SO created, update it and save

The problem is that in a multi-company environment, we cannot access
the warehouse of a different company. In the sale_order model, the
`_init_column` method populates the warehouse value for existing sales
orders before stock is installed. It uses self.env.company to set
the warehouse, but `_init_column` is called with superuser privileges,
which lack user context. This causes warehouses to always be linked to

body:
## preview Note that when using the preview version of AL-Go for GitHub, we recommend you Update your AL-Go system files, as soon as possible when informed that an update is available. ### Security - Add top-level permissions for _Increment Version Number_ workflow ### Issues - Issue 1697 Error in CheckForUpdates: "Internet Explorer engine is not available" when using self-hosted runners - Issue 1685 HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration ### Workflow input validation Some workflow inputs are now validated early in order to avoid workflows to make modifications like creating a release, when we already should know that an error will occur later. ### Test settings against a JSON schema AL-Go for GitHub settings now has a schema. The following line is added at the beginning to any AL-Go settings files to utilize the schema: ``` "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/AL-Go-Actions//Actions/settings.schema.json" ``` ### Failing pull requests if new warnings are added By setting failOn to 'newWarning', pull requests will fail if new warnings are introduced. This feature compares the warnings in the pull request build against those in the latest successful CI/CD build and fails if new warnings are detected. ## v7.1 ### Issues - Issue 1678 Test summary is showing too many status icons - Issue 1640 AL1040 error due to app folder within the artifacts cache being incorrectly recognized as an app folder - Issue 1630 Error when downloading a release, when the destination folder already exists. - Issue 1540 and 1649 Apps with dependencies to Microsft\_\_EXCLUDE\_ apps fails deployment - Issue 1547 Dependencies will be installed even if DependencyInstallMode is ignore, but dependencies will never be installed on production environments - Issue 1654 GithubPackageContext does not work together with private trustedNuGetFeeds - Issue 1627 AL-Go should throw an error or a warning if you create a release, which is older than the latest release - Issue 1657 When no files modified on Git, deployment fails - Issue 1530 Dependency Field Service Integration does not get published in container while Installing apps - Issue 1644 Support for AppAuth when using a private Template repository from another organization - Issue 1669 GitHub App authentication to download dependencies from private repositories - Issue 1478 Rate Limit Exceeded when running Update AL-Go System files ## v7.0 ### Issues - Issue 1519 Submitting to AppSource WARNING: AuthContext.Scopes is .. should be - Issue 1521 Dependencies not installed for multi project incremental PR build - Issue 1522 Strange warnings in Deploy job post update to AL-Go 6.4 - BcContainerHelper settings were only read from .github/AL-Go-Settings.json, not allowing global settings in ALGoOrgSettings for TrustedNuGetFeeds, MemoryLimit and other things that should be possible to define globally - Issue 1526 When updating AL-Go system files, the update process (creating a PR or directly pushing to the branch) fails when there is a file or directory in the repo with the same name as the branch that is to be updated - Legacy code signing stopped working ### Page Scripting visualizer Page scripting tests have been available for AL-Go for GitHub for a while but required manual inspection of the Page scripting artifact to see the results. It is now possible to get a quick overview in the job summary section of a CICD build, similar to how regular and bcpt test results are displayed. No new settings are required. Test results will automatically be displayed if tests are enabled via the existing setting [pageScriptingTests](https://aka.ms/algosettings#pageScriptingTests). ### Support for deploying to sandbox environments from a pull request AL-Go for GitHub now supports deploying from a PR. When using the 'Publish To Environment' workflow, it is now possible to input 'PR_X' as the App version, where 'X' is the PR Id. This will deploy the artifacts from the latest PR build to the chosen environment, if that build is completed and successful. All apps, which were not built by the PR build will be deployed from the last known good build. You can find a notification on the PR build explaining which build is used as the last known good build. > [!NOTE] > When deploying a PR build to a sandbox environment, the app will get a special version number, which is: major.minor.maxint.run-number. This means that the sandbox environment likely needs to be deleted after the testing has ended. ## v6.4 ### Deprecations - `alwaysBuildAllProjects` will be removed after October 1st 2025. Please set the `onPull_Request` property of the `incrementalBuilds` setting to false to force full builds in Pull Requests. - `Schedule` will be removed after October 1st 2025. The old setting, where the setting key was a combination of the workflow name and `Schedule` (dynamic setting key name) is deprecated. Instead you need to use a setting called [workflowSchedule](https://aka.ms/algosettings#workflowSchedule) and either use [Conditional Settings](https://aka.ms/algosettings#conditional-settings) or place the setting in a workflow specific settings file. ### Issues - Issue 1433 Publish to Environment - DependencyInstallMode not found - Issue 1440 Create Release fails due to recent changes to the AL-Go - Issue 1330 CompilerFolder doesn't transfer installed Apps to NuGet resolution - Issue 1268 Do not throw an un-understandable error during nuGet download - Performance test sample code in 25.4 contains objects with ID 149201 and 149202, which are not renumbered - Issue 798 Publish To Environment breaks CI/CD pipelines - Issue 1182 Runs-on setting type is ambiguous - string or array - Issue 1502 NuGet dependency version is always LatestMatching ### New Workflow specific settings - `workflowSchedule` - can be structure with a property named `cron`, which must be a valid crontab, defining the CRON schedule for when the specified workflow should run. Default is no scheduled runs, only manual triggers. Build your crontab string here: [https://crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru). You need to run the Update AL-Go System Files workflow for the schedule to take effect.
**Note:** If you configure a WorkflowSchedule for the CI/CD workflow, AL-Go will stop triggering CICDs on push unless you have also added CICDPushBranches to your settings.
**Note also:** If you define a schedule for Update AL-Go System Files, it uses direct Commit instead of creating a PR. - `workflowConcurrency` - is used to control concurrency of workflows. Like with the `workflowSchedule` setting, this setting should be applied in workflow specific settings files or conditional settings. By default, all workflows allows for concurrency, except for the Create Release workflow. If you are using incremental builds in CI/CD it is also recommented to set WorkflowConcurrency to:
`[ "group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}", "cancel-in-progress: true" ]`
in order to cancel prior incremental builds on the same branch.
Read more about workflow concurrency [here](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/control-the-concurrency-of-workflows-and-jobs). ### New Repository Settings - `nuGetFeedSelectMode` determines the select mode when finding Business Central app packages from NuGet feeds, based on the dependency version specified in app.json. author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
PR #27096: Add a pass that removes degenerate dimensions from all-gathers. 

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/27096

`GpuLayoutAssignment` requires all-gathers to gather on the major dimension (i.e., the gathered tensor is contiguous). When we have a pattern like `all-gather(dynamic-slice)` and the slice's major dimension is degenerate, the all-gather gets a funky non-standard layout, which is then propagated through the slice, ultimately all the way to the parameter, where we eventually introduce a transposing copy. See https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/26987 for details.

This should fix about 2/3 of that bug. The remaining transposing copies are caused by all-gathers that actually need to be transposes, but the fix for those is more complicated.


Copybara import of the project:

--
4c817c55329fc4139451db14aea2d66bab737496 by Johannes Reifferscheid <jreiffers@nvidia.com>:

[WIP] Add a pass that removes degenerate dimensions from all-gathers.

Not really tested yet.

--
a3f042ab9f90bdb0d85f3f9207d9b35b8e9a1c6b by Johannes Reifferscheid <jreiffers@nvidia.com>:

Add tests.

--
66a336e21233cfc6771044cdebb5b45fad747ba0 by Johannes Reifferscheid <jreiffers@nvidia.com>:

Fix unused status.

--
6c5dbb46d660cf24723c422cdaecb8dbb774d5e5 by Johannes Reifferscheid <jreiffers@nvidia.com>:

Fix missing newline at end of file.

--
8d124d55f700e4a764a9fd4b18167be50d18b214 by Johannes Reifferscheid <jreiffers@nvidia.com>:

Add support for tuple all-gathers.

These are quite a bit more complicated because they can have mixed shapes.
We can drop all degenerate dimenions that are more minor than the all_gather_dim.

For more major dimensions, we only drop them if they are degenerate in all
operands. Technically, we could drop them if the number of degenerate dims
matches (but not necessarily the indices), but that seems a bit excessive.

Merging this change closes #27096

author: mingnus
body:
This pull request addresses issues related to the passthrough mode in the dm-cache module of the Linux kernel. The changes focus on enhancing thread safety and refining the cache invalidation logic. 

In `drivers/md/dm-cache-policy-smq.c`, a spinlock mechanism (`spin_lock_irqsave`/`spin_unlock_irqrestore`) is introduced in the `smq_invalidate_mapping` function to protect shared data structures such as queues, hash tables, and allocator entries from concurrent access during cache entry invalidation.

In `drivers/md/dm-cache-target.c`, the cache invalidation logic is refactored to improve the handling of `overwrite_bio` and the sequence of metadata commits relative to bio submissions. The changes include the addition of `invalidate_retry` for managing cell lock failures and `invalidate_committed` to ensure bios are processed only after metadata changes are committed. Additionally, a bug fix in `map_bio` ensures correct termination of processing for bios handled by `invalidate_start` in passthrough mode.

- **TenantContext**: Created a context provider for organization-specific data, user roles, and language preferences

author: emeroad
body:
This pull request refactors the `MapServiceImpl` class in `web/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/web/applicationmap/service/MapServiceImpl.java` to improve code readability and modularity. Key changes include introducing a new method for handling cases with no request data, simplifying method signatures, and modifying factory methods to accept boolean parameters instead of `MapServiceOption`.

### Refactoring for improved modularity:

* **Introduced `buildForNoRequest` method**: Added a private method to handle scenarios where no nodes are found in the application map, ensuring the map is still built with the source application. This improves readability and encapsulates logic.

### Simplification of method signatures:

* **Refactored `newNodeHistogramFactory` method**: Changed the method to accept a boolean parameter (`isSimpleResponseHistogram`) instead of the entire `MapServiceOption` object, simplifying its usage.
* **Refactored `newServerGroupListFactory` method**: Updated the method to accept a boolean parameter (`isUseStatisticsAgentState`) instead of `MapServiceOption`, aligning with the changes made to `newNodeHistogramFactory`.

### Code cleanup and minor adjustments:

* **Modified `selectApplicationMap` logic**: Replaced direct calls to `builder.build` with the new `buildForNoRequest` method for handling empty nodes, improving clarity.
* **Added import for `Application`**: Included the necessary import for the `Application` class to support the new `buildForNoRequest` method.

author: olemartinorg
body:
## Description

I recently added a few `Summary2` components to `ttd/frontend-test` which references all the previous tasks. When doing that, I noticed a few errors in DevTools that weren't there before. It turns out that two unanticipated things happened here:

1. The `Effect*` components were rendered inside the node hierarchy, which caused one of the components to try to set `preselectedOptionIndex` in the database. Since the data model here belonged to a previous task and was locked, `FormDataWrite` stopped to attempt with an error. This PR prevents these effects from running at all when in a "read only" state such as rendering for Summary2.
2. If an embedded layout-set sets up dynamics, i.e. rules that run via javascript objects, loading the javascript could end up overwriting dynamics for the parent FormProvider and ruining dynamics there. This can happen if set up in a subform layout-set, but also if rendered via Summary2 pointing to a previous task. This PR adds an error to the DevTools about this, and refuses to run rules in embedded `FormProvider`.

I still have left to check existing apps and who might be affected by this slight change. I should inform app developers that have set up dynamics when using FormProvider embedding, in addition to documenting when doing such doesn't work as one might think.

This pull request introduces significant updates to the `sanitizr` project, marking its transition from early development to a stable release. The changes include adding a workflow for publishing to PyPI, updating the project's version and status, and improving the CLI with a version flag. Additionally, the documentation has been updated to reflect the availability of the package on PyPI.

### PyPI Publishing Workflow:
* [`.github/workflows/publish.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-551d1fcf87f78cc3bc18a7b332a4dc5d8773a512062df881c5aba28a6f5c48d7R1-R36): Added a GitHub Actions workflow to automate publishing the package to PyPI when a new version tag is pushed to the main branch.

### Project Version and Stability:
* [`pyproject.toml`](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L8-R8): Updated the version from `0.1.0` to `1.0.0` and changed the development status classifier from "Alpha" to "Production/Stable." [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L8-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L17-R17)
* `sanitizr/__init__.py` and `sanitizr/cleanurl/__init__.py`: Updated the hardcoded fallback version to `1.0.0` to align with the stable release. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e337fa115d26f63e5e969c0a8774b186b323c132ca764e5f4147f9f57066515bL12-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-215ad628988a1a65dd3c025652bb843fa86b149e81a78374bf812c8248ff4316L16-R16)

### CLI Improvements:
* [`sanitizr/cleanurl/cli/__main__.py`](diffhunk://#diff-4d49387a748aef0e61b8ec78841303abb9de1ce7aaf4e4ce42c2cb5fe2f81bfeR59-R65): Added a `--version` flag to the CLI for displaying the program's version number.

### Documentation Updates:
* [`README.md`](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L6-R6): Removed references to early development and updated installation instructions to reflect the availability of the package on PyPI. author: inbalben-lulu
body:
This PR implements full mail and label management functionality, integrating user-level access control, blacklist enforcement via a C++ TCP server, and dynamic label handling.

Mail Management 
Implemented full flow for sending, retrieving, updating, deleting, and searching mails:
- mailStorage.js – Stores mails and maps them to user inboxes
- mailModel.js – Core business logic: filtering, formatting, blacklist checking
- mailController.js – API logic, input validation, status codes
- mailRoute.js – Defines /api/mails endpoints with middleware enforcement

Label Support
Implemented user-specific label creation, retrieval, renaming, and deletion:
- labelStorage.js – In-memory label mapping per user
- labelModel.js – Validations, ID management, uniqueness enforcement
- labelController.js – Handles API input/output and response codes
- labelRoute.js – Routes under /api/labels with middleware validation

User Header Validation Middleware 
Added validateUserHeader.js middleware:
- Extracts and verifies userId from request headers
- Validates user existence via getUserById
- Handles malformed/missing headers with appropriate status codes (400/404)

Full Integration with Blacklist Server
All mail creation and update operations enforce URL safety via:
- Asynchronous TCP socket communication with the C++ blacklist server
- Use of sendToBlacklistServer() and parallel GET checks
- Server returns null or -1 if blacklisted links are detected
- Consistent user feedback via 400 errors for blocked content

body:
Implement a comprehensive open-source economic simulation engine with transparent, auditable financial risk modeling capabilities for research and public institutions.

BREAKING CHANGE: Initial release of jinn-core platform

Features:
- Core simulation engine with model registry and JSON configuration
- Interest rate shock model for Federal Reserve policy simulation
- Inflation shock model for supply chain disruption analysis
- Comprehensive mathematical utilities and output formatting
- 28 comprehensive tests with 100% pass rate
- Complete documentation and developer guides
- Automated setup and validation scripts
- Working demo and example scenarios

Components Added:
- src/engine.py: Main simulation orchestration system
- src/models/interest_rate.py: Fed rate shock economic model
- src/models/inflation_shock.py: Supply chain inflation model
- src/utils/: Mathematical and formatting utilities
- tests/test_engine.py: Complete test suite (28 tests)
- examples/: Federal Reserve and inflation crisis scenarios
- docs/: Comprehensive documentation and developer guides
- setup.sh: Automated environment setup script
- validate.py: Project health validation system
- demo.py: Interactive demonstration

Technical Details:
- Python 3.8+ compatibility with type hints throughout
- NumPy vectorization for mathematical operations
- JSON-based scenario configuration system
- Modular architecture for easy model extension
- Professional error handling and logging
- Virtual environment support with dependency management

Documentation:
- README.md: Complete user guide with examples
- DEVELOPMENT.md: Comprehensive developer documentation
- PROJECT_STATUS.md: Current capabilities and roadmap
- Inline documentation with Google-style docstrings

Testing & Quality:
- 100% test pass rate (28 comprehensive test cases)
- Automated validation with 38 health checks
- PEP 8 compliance with full type annotation coverage
- Production-ready code quality standards

Examples:
- Federal Reserve 75bp rate hike simulation
- Supply chain 5pp inflation spike analysis
- Custom scenario creation capabilities

This establishes jinn-core as a transparent, community-driven platform for economic foresight analysis, providing open-source alternatives to proprietary financial modeling tools.

author: mhuisi
body:
This PR implements signature help support. When typing a function application, editors with support for signature help will now display a popup that designates the current (remaining) function type. This removes the need to remember the function signature while typing the function application, or having to constantly cycle between hovering over the function identifier and typing the application. In VS Code, the signature help can be triggered manually using `Ctrl+Shift+Space`.

![Demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1f6ed79-bb16-4593-8d28-68b1cce5d5dc)

### Other changes

- In order to support signature help for the partial syntax `f a <|` or `f a $`, these notations now elaborate as `f a`, not `f a .missing`.
- The logic in `delabConstWithSignature` that delaborates parameters is factored out into a function `delabForallParamsWithSignature` so that it can be used for arbitrary `forall`s, not just constants.
- The `InfoTree` formatter is adjusted to produce output where it is easier to identify the kind of `Info` in the `InfoTree`.
- A bug in `InfoTree.smallestInfo?` is fixed so that it doesn't panic anymore when its predicate `p` does not ensure that both `pos?` and `tailPos?` of the `Info` are present.

author: packerlschupfer
body:
## Summary

This PR consolidates multiple improvements to the esp32ModbusRTU library:

### Bug Fixes
- Fix FC2 byte count calculation (ceiling division per Modbus spec)
- Fix FC 05/06 response data extraction
- Add DE/RE turnaround delay after TX flush for RS-485 reliability

### New Function Codes
- FC 0x01 (Read Coils)
- FC 0x05 (Write Single Coil)
- FC 0x0F (Write Multiple Coils)
- FC 0x17 (Read/Write Multiple Registers)

### Memory Safety
- Add configurable MODBUS_TASK_STACK_SIZE and MODBUS_TASK_PRIORITY
- Add null queue validation to prevent crashes
- Add bounds checking with MODBUS_MAX_REGISTERS/MODBUS_MAX_COILS limits
- Add INVALID_PARAMETER, QUEUE_FULL, MEMORY_ALLOCATION_FAILED error types

### Watchdog Timer Support
- Add ESP32 Task Watchdog Timer (TWDT) support
- Add MODBUS_DISABLE_WATCHDOG build flag to disable
- Add setWatchdogEnabled()/isWatchdogEnabled() runtime control

### Priority Queue System
- Replace single FIFO with 4 priority queues (EMERGENCY/SENSOR/RELAY/STATUS)
- Add *WithPriority() variants for all read/write methods
- Legacy API defaults to RELAY priority for backward compatibility

### Logging System
- Add esp32ModbusRTULogging.h with flexible logging configuration
- Default: ESP-IDF logging with zero overhead (debug compiled out)
- Development: Define MODBUS_RTU_DEBUG for protocol tracing
- Optional: Define USE_CUSTOM_LOGGER for custom Logger integration

## Test Plan
- [ ] Verify FC2 byte count calculation
- [ ] Test new function codes (FC 0x01, 0x05, 0x0F, 0x17)
- [ ] Verify priority queue ordering
- [ ] Test watchdog enable/disable
- [ ] Verify backward compatibility with existing code

author: alanpicarrot
body:
Added @Transactional to the `registerUser` method in `UserAuthServiceImpl.java`. This ensures that the creation of a new user and the assignment of their default roles (specifically ROLE_USER) are part of a single, atomic database transaction.

This change aims to resolve potential data visibility issues where a newly registered user's roles might not be immediately available to a subsequent login attempt, which could lead to authorization failures (e.g., 401) when accessing protected resources that require ROLE_USER.

author: jorainer
body:
I think it would be best to split the `symmetric_dotproduct_combined()` functions into two separate functions, one that maps/matches the peaks between the compared spectra and one that calculates the similarity. With that it should be possible to use the similarity calculation directly in `Spectra::compareSpectra()` and `MetaboAnnotation::matchSpectra()` functions - including the reporting of the number of matched peaks.

So, the first function `dynlib_map()` I started to sketch down would take the input peak matrices `x` and `y` as well as `xPrecursorMz` and `yPrecursorMz` as input parameters and would return a `list` of 2 peak matrices that contains **only** the matching peaks.

The result of the function should look like e.g.

```r
$x
      [,1] [,2]
[1,]  12.5  100
[2,] 100.0  200

$y
      [,1] [,2]
[1,]  12.5  150
[2,] 100.0  200
```

i.e. be a `list` with elements `x` and `y` and each of them being a `matrix` with the m/z in the first and intensity values in the second column.

That could then be passed to the second function that calculates the similarity score based on these. @Ahlammentag , check also the comments I mode in the code for more info.

author: silto
body:
# Contexte

## GraphQL

Ajout du registre exhaustif en V2, avec une API et interface cohérente avec Registres V2
- mutation de génération d'export `generateRegistryExhaustiveExport`
- query de listing des exports exhaustifs `registryExhaustiveExports`
- query de récupération d'un export unique `registryExhaustiveExport`
- query de récupération d'un URL de fichier d'export `registryExhaustiveExportDownloadSignedUrl`

Afin de mettre à jour l'interface d'export de registre destinée aux admins, ajout de queries/mutation admin:
- registryV2ExportsAsAdmin
- registryExhaustiveExportsAsAdmin
- generateRegistryV2ExportAsAdmin
- generateRegistryExhaustiveExportAsAdmin

-> leur resolver est le même que les queries non admin, avec juste un paramètre pour signaler qu'elles sont utilisées en tant qu'admin.

Ca permet l'ajout d'un flag sur les exports ("asAdmin") pour ne pas mélanger les exports de leurs entreprises et les exports en tant qu'admin dans les tableaux des admins.

## Fonctionnement

Le fonctionnement interne est le même que celui des registres V2, à part une différence importante: on utilise l'index elastic comme source des bordereaux à renvoyer au lieu de la table RegistryLookup. Ce choix est dû au fait que le registre exhaustif ne contient que les bordereaux, et qu'il se doit d'être cohérent avec le dashboard. Toutes les informations étant donc dans elastic, rien ne sert d'ajouter plein de lignes à la table RegistryLookup qui est déjà bien chargée.

Le résultat du registre exhaustif est revu, que ce soit au niveau des colonnes qui se voient harmonisées avec les colonnes des registres V2, ainsi que pour ce qui est des critère d'inclusion des bordereaux. En effet, les bordereaux n'apparaissaient auparavant dans ce registre qu'à partir de la signature transporteur, alors qu'ils apparaissent maintenant à partir de leur publication.

Afin de ne pas modifier le fonctionnement des exports V1 qui sont gardés pour l'instant, ajout d'une colonne elastic (isExhaustiveWasteFor). Il y a donc une montée de version de elastic, et il faut faire un reindex.

## Frontend

Afin de générer les différents types d'export (Réglementaire, Exhaustif, Réglementaire en tant qu'admin, Exhaustif en tant qu'admin) sans recopier des composants, j'ai déplacé la logique spécifique dans des componsants de contexte. Ainsi il suffit de wrapper MyExports (et la modale d'export qui est un de ces enfants) dans des composants de contexte pour adapter son comportement au registre V2 ou exhaustif, en tant qu'admin ou non :
```ts
// mode Registre V2 + admin
<RegistryV2ExportProvider asAdmin={true}>
  <RegistryV2ExportModalProvider asAdmin={true}>
    <MyExports />
  </RegistryV2ExportModalProvider>
</RegistryV2ExportProvider>

// mode Registre Exhaustif + non admin
<RegistryExhaustiveExportProvider>
  <RegistryExhaustiveExportModalProvider>
    <MyExports />
  </RegistryExhaustiveExportModalProvider>
</RegistryExhaustiveExportProvider>
```

# Points de vigilance pour les intégrateurs

Les queries de registre V1 restent valides et continuent de fonctionner de la même façon, mais une mention "deprecated" y a été ajoutée en vue de leur disparition prochaine.

# Démo

Export exhaustif

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7288f7b4-922e-475a-b10b-25658709939d

Export V2 et exhaustif admin

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44359316-840c-48c3-9951-53cc1349bd77



# Ticket Favro
[Mettre le registre exhaustif en V2](https://favro.com/organization/ab14a4f0460a99a9d64d4945/2c84e07578945e0ee8fb61f3?card=tra-16217)
[Agrémenter le registre exhaustif dès la publication de chaque bordereau](https://favro.com/organization/ab14a4f0460a99a9d64d4945/2c84e07578945e0ee8fb61f3?card=tra-16218)
